analysis: Examined release-provider.yml base lines 1–1066 and the complete changed-range map/patch. The changes add workflow-wide DARKBLOOM_PROVIDER_TOOLCHAIN=release (head 114) and update the retained validation identity's expected SDK from 27.0 to 27.2 (head 1444). Neither change visibly weakens source gating, artifact binding, signing, entitlements, notarization or authorization. Relevant contracts include A-011/A-017 and T-034/T-054 for exact build identity, and TB-003/TB-009 for hardened runtime and key access. The supplied surrounding workflow gates signing on build and SDK qualification (base 325–331), validates unsigned source/version (457–460), verifies signed entitlements (713–767), checks final signed archive bytes and full CodeDirectory hash (878–995), and removes the signing keychain before cluster-facts execution (1014–1030). These controls are outside the mapped changes; no supported regression was identified here. Integration must verify how the new environment variable is consumed by scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh and .github/actions/provider-release-build, including qualification, resumed builds and the older-macOS validation lane. Their implementations and the validation lane's surrounding source are not supplied in these units, so alignment of build/sign SDK selection with the new 27.2 assertion remains unverified. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a missing control. No inference encryption, billing or consumer-data handling changes are visible in this scope.
